base_properties.human_readable: Feud-Obligation Suppression via Christianized Pacification (Ecclesiastical Authority Reading)

perspectives.label: The Feud Participant (Kinship-Bound)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 1: FEUD PARTICIPANT (SNARE) — Identity is constituted through kinship obligation and blood-debt. Church doctrine declares vengeance sinful, yet kinship honor demands retaliation. The participant is structurally mobile (could refuse) but identity-locked: exiting the feud requires abandoning family identity and honor. Suppression is enforced through spiritual peril (damnation, excommunication) combined with social ostracism. High effective extraction — the constraint extracts full participation while simultaneously declaring that participation is sin.

perspectives.label: The Kinship Group (Collective Obligation)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 2: KINSHIP GROUP (TANGLED ROPE) — Feud coordination solves a real collective action problem: absent centralized enforcement, blood-debt retaliation is the only mechanism to deter predation and protect group interests. Church doctrine undermines this coordination while offering no alternative enforcement mechanism. Suppression is high (excommunication, penance requirements, spiritual penalties) but the constraint has genuine coordination function (deterrence, group defense). Constrained exit: leaving exposes the group to undefended predation.

perspectives.label: The Ecclesiastical Authority
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 3: ECCLESIASTICAL AUTHORITY (ROPE) — Church gains interpretive monopoly over legitimate violence and expanded jurisdictional reach through the doctrine that vengeance belongs to God alone, delegated to episcopal courts and royal authority. From Church perspective, the constraint is coordination: rerouting violence through penitential discipline and ecclesiastical arbitration consolidates clerical power while ostensibly reducing disorder. Benefits from expanded confession-based surveillance, penitential authority, and role as arbiter of legitimate vs. sinful violence. Arbitrage exit: Church can shift enforcement intensity without losing core benefit.

perspectives.label: The Royal Authority
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 4: ROYAL AUTHORITY (ROPE) — Crown benefits from Church doctrine that private feud violates divine law. Doctrine provides legitimacy for royal monopoly on violence and prohibition of private retaliation. From monarch perspective, constraint is coordination: converting blood-debt obligation into obligation to seek royal arbitration concentrates enforcement authority in crown courts rather than kinship networks. Arbitrage exit: throne can relax or intensify suppression based on political needs without losing coordination function.

perspectives.label: The Peace Guild / Urban Coalition
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 5: PEACE GUILD / URBAN COALITION (SCAFFOLD) — Organized urban merchants and town authorities institute peace guilds and mutual-defense associations that provide alternative deterrence mechanisms to feuding. These replace blood-debt retaliation with contractual bonding and collective enforcement through guild law (e.g., Hanseatic League, Italian podestà). This perspective sees feud-suppression constraint as temporary, with sunset driven by rise of urban commercial networks that solve deterrence problem without kinship obligation. Low theater because guild enforcement mechanisms are functionally effective at their stated goal (protecting commerce without feud cycles). Sunset horizon: 150-250 years as urban institutional density increases.

perspectives.label: The Nobility (Dual Authority)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 6: NOBILITY (TANGLED ROPE) — Noble houses simultaneously hold feud obligations (kinship honor) and royal authority delegated through crown. They coordinate the suppression of lower-status feuding while reserving higher-status feud rights (border raids, dynastic conflicts). Constraint has genuine coordination function (managed feuding preserves deterrence while channeling violence toward crown-approved targets) and asymmetric extraction (commoners bear suppression; nobility retains status-stratified violence rights). Constrained exit: maintaining dual authority requires continued enforcement against lower orders.

perspectives.label: The Parish Priest (Ritualizing Authority)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 7: PARISH PRIEST (PITON) — Local clergy maintain confession, penance, and excommunication procedures that theoretically enforce the feud-suppression doctrine. In practice, enforcement is highly theatrical: confessional secrets are kept, penances are negotiated, excommunications are routinely absolved through payment or political pressure. The priest's authority has degraded into ritualistic maintenance of the suppression apparatus while actual participation in feuding continues. Theater ratio is high because the enforcement machinery (confession, absolution cycles) persists through institutional inertia despite low functional verification of actual behavior change. Arbitrage exit: priests can adjust enforcement intensity without losing clerical status.

perspectives.label: Theological Natural Law View (False Summit Risk)
perspectives.comment: PERSPECTIVE 8: ANALYTICAL OBSERVER / THEOLOGICAL NATURAL LAW VIEW (MOUNTAIN) — From a civilizational/universal perspective, the claim that vengeance belongs to God alone and must be forbidden is presented as a moral law grounded in divine command and universal Christian doctrine. This perspective treats feud-suppression as an unchangeable law of Christendom, derived from immutable theological principle. However, the structural data contradicts the mountain classification: identifiable beneficiaries (Church, Crown), specific enforcement mechanisms (confession, excommunication, royal courts), and contingent historical timing (doctrine emerges 11th-12th centuries in response to specific regional feuding patterns) all indicate a constructed constraint, not a natural law. The engine will flag this as a false summit revealing that theological naturalization obscures power consolidation.

omegas.question: Is the tension between kinship honor-obligation and Church doctrine prohibiting vengeance genuinely unresolvable, or can feud participants reconcile them through doctrinal reinterpretation?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Historical analysis of confessional manuals, penitential practices, and documented feud participation by nominally Christian families. Detection of doctrinal reinterpretations that permit blood-debt obligation as legitimate self-defense rather than sinful vengeance.
omegas.impact: If unresolvable: identity_locked classification is correct — participants face genuine cognitive impossibility of reconciling identities. If reconcilable: exit_options should shift to constrained (high cost but thinkable) rather than identity_locked. Reclassifies snare perspective to tangled_rope.
omegas.description: Whether kinship honor and Christian doctrine are doctrinally irreconcilable

omegas.question: Do ecclesiastical enforcement mechanisms (confession-based surveillance, excommunication, penance) actually reduce feud participation rates, or do participants engage in parallel observance (confess, do penance, continue feuding)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparison of feud frequency before and after intensive ecclesiastical enforcement campaigns. Analysis of confessional records (where available) and court documents showing reported vs. actual behavior compliance. Regional variation correlating Church institutional density with feud rates.
omegas.impact: If enforcement is efficacious: suppression (0.72) is correct as measured. If enforcement is theater: true suppression is lower, and suppression measurement should reflect only non-theatrical barriers (kinship obligation itself, not institutional enforcement). Reclassifies from tangled_rope toward rope for institutional beneficiaries; theater_ratio should increase.
omegas.description: Whether ecclesiastical enforcement mechanisms actually reduce feud participation

omegas.question: Are dual authorities (Church and Crown) genuinely cooperative in suppressing feuding, or do they compete for enforcement monopoly in ways that undermine suppression?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Analysis of documented conflicts between episcopal and royal jurisdiction over feud cases. Examination of cases where Church and Crown ruled differently on feud legitimacy. Detection of periods where competition for authority escalated rather than reduced feuding.
omegas.impact: If cooperative: royal and ecclesiastical beneficiary perspectives are aligned, suppression is stable. If competitive: suppression effectiveness deteriorates during periods of Church-Crown conflict, and the constraint may decompose into separate Church-centric and Crown-centric stories with different ε values and competing beneficiaries.
omegas.description: Whether Church and Crown authorities cooperate or compete in feud suppression

omegas.question: Is the theological claim that vengeance belongs to God alone a universal principle of Christendom, or a specific doctrinal development responding to 11th-12th century feuding patterns in particular regions?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Historical analysis of doctrine emergence: comparison of pre-11th-century Christian theology on violence (Augustine, just war theory) with 12th-century elaboration (Gratian, scholasticism). Regional variation in doctrine adoption correlating with feuding intensity and ecclesiastical institutional density. Identification of alternative Christian theologies permitting private retaliation (Eastern Orthodox, Coptic, heterodox communities).
omegas.impact: If universal principle: mountain classification is correct. If contingent doctrinal development: false summit diagnosis is confirmed, constraint is tangled_rope with extractive beneficiary structure, and treating it as natural law obscures power consolidation. This is the core committer ambiguity: is the kernel (vengeance belongs to God) discovered or constructed?
omegas.description: Whether feud-suppression doctrine is universal Christian principle or contingent institutional development

omegas.question: Is identity-locking to kinship obligation uniform across social ranks, or do lower-status participants experience weaker identity fusion while nobility maintain strong honor identity?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative analysis of confessional self-reports, court testimony, and documented behavior across rank groups. Detection of differential language around honor, shame, and obligation in sources stratified by social status.
omegas.impact: If uniform: identity_locked exit option applies across feud participants. If stratified: nobility use identity_locked framing to justify feuding while lower ranks experience constrained or trapped exit; classification shifts from uniform to rank-specific, requiring separate perspectives for commoner vs. noble feuding.
omegas.description: Whether identity-locking to kinship obligation is socially uniform

omegas.question: Is this constraint measuring the theological doctrine (prohibition of vengeance), the institutional enforcement apparatus (Church and Crown courts), or the behavioral outcome (actual feud rates)? Does the kernel shift if measured differently?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Decomposition test: author separate constraint stories for (a) doctrine as formalized claim, (b) ecclesiastical enforcement apparatus, (c) crown authority consolidation, (d) measured feud behavior. Compare ε values across the four stories. If ε values differ significantly (> 0.15), the kernel is observable-dependent and multiple constraints are operating.
omegas.impact: This is the core ε-invariance principle test. If different observables produce different ε values, this story has actually collapsed multiple constraints into one. Expected outcome: doctrine story (pure Rope, ε~0.15), enforcement apparatus story (Tangled Rope, ε~0.48), behavioral suppression story (Snare, ε~0.72). Current story targets behavioral suppression. Document in network.affects_constraints and dual_formulation_note if decomposition is needed.
omegas.description: Observable-dependence test: kernel shifts if measured at doctrine vs. enforcement vs. outcome level

commentary.narrative_context: This constraint story instantiates the CHRISTIANIZED PACIFICATION READING of the feud-obligation kernel. The kernel itself — whether blood-debt obligation can coexist with Christian prohibition of vengeance — is contested across three readings with structurally distinct ε values and beneficiary/victim configurations. THIS reading measures the constraint as it operates under the theological/institutional claim that feud participation violates divine law and legitimate violence authority is delegated to Church and Crown alone. From this reading's perspective, all feud participants enter the victim set (spiritual peril, suppression risk) while ecclesiastical and royal authorities enter the beneficiary set (interpretive monopoly, jurisdictional expansion). The constraint exhibits high theater (ritual penance and confession maintaining suppression despite low behavioral efficacy), moderate extractiveness (Church and Crown benefit; kinship obligation is suppressed but not eliminated), and high suppression (multiple enforcement mechanisms: spiritual penalty, excommunication, royal prosecution). The identity-locked exit option for feud participants reflects that kinship honor-obligation is constitutive of social identity — exit would require ceasing to be recognizable as a family member within the kinship structure. This is qualitatively different from constrained or trapped exit: the participant could theoretically refuse retaliation, but doing so dissolves their identity within the kinship frame. The measurements show institutional inertia: theater increases over the interval (confession and penance become more formulaic, less behaviorally consequential) while extractiveness and suppression requirement gradually rise as enforcement infrastructure matures. The constraint transitions from nascent doctrinal claim (low theater, moderate suppression) toward mature institutional apparatus (high theater, high suppression) characteristic of a tangled_rope degrading toward piton.
key_agents: Feud Participant (Kinship-Bound): Primary victim (powerless/identity_locked) — identity is constituted through kinship obligation; exit is identity-dissolving; bears spiritual and legal suppression
Kinship Group: Secondary victim (moderate/constrained) — feud coordination solves real deterrence problem; suppression undermines group defense without providing alternative

Ecclesiastical Authority: Primary beneficiary (institutional/arbitrage) — gains interpretive monopoly over legitimate violence, expanded confession-based surveillance, jurisdictional authority through penitential discipline
Royal Authority: Primary beneficiary (institutional/arbitrage) — gains monopoly on legitimate violence, concentration of enforcement authority in crown courts, delegated divine sanction
Nobility (Dual Authority): Mixed (organized/constrained) — coordinate suppression of lower-status feuding while reserving status-stratified violence rights for themselves
Peace Guild / Urban Coalition: Organized opponent (organized/constrained) — offers alternative deterrence mechanisms; constrains feud suppression's duration through competing institutional solutions
Parish Priest: Ritualist (institutional/arbitrage) — maintains performative enforcement apparatus; low behavioral efficacy; permits parallel feuding participation through confession mechanics

Analytical Observer: External perspective (analytical/analytical) — risks naturalizing contingent institutional arrangement (Church-Crown alliance for violence monopoly) as universal theological principle
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness (0.58): Moderate-high. Church and Crown extract significant benefit from feud suppression: ecclesiastical authority gains interpretive monopoly and jurisdictional reach; royal authority gains violence monopoly and delegated divine sanction. However, extractiveness is not maximal (0.72+) because a genuine coordination function remains: feud suppression does reduce uncontrolled violence cycles and does provide alternative dispute resolution (penitential discipline, royal courts). The constraint genuinely solves a problem (disorder from unlimited retaliation) while concentrating authority in institutions that benefit from providing the solution. The measurement trajectory shows extractiveness rising as institutional maturity increases and coordination function becomes standardized — early enforcement relies more on doctrine; later enforcement relies on established procedures. Suppression (0.72): High. Multiple enforcement mechanisms operate simultaneously: spiritual peril (damnation, excommunication), social penalty (community ostracism for those who violate doctrine), legal penalty (royal prosecution for defiance of crown authority), and internalized guilt (confession mechanics). The combination creates high suppression despite low actual behavioral efficacy — participants find ways to participate while appearing compliant. Theater ratio (0.68): Moderate-high and rising. Confession and penance are performative: penitents confess violence intentions or actions, receive absolution or penance, then continue feuding. The ritual maintenance of compliance exceeds actual behavioral change. Theater increases over the interval because as institutional procedures become standardized, they are practiced more formulaically — confessors become routinized, penances become negotiable through donations, absolution becomes automatic. The early constraint (low theater, high behavioral intent) transitions to late constraint (high theater, low behavioral change) — a characteristic piton trajectory. Claimed type tangled_rope is correct at the interval endpoint because the constraint retains genuine coordination function (reduces uncontrolled violence) while extracting significant institutional benefit — it is not pure extraction (snare) because actors retain some choice and some coordination benefit, nor is it pure coordination (rope) because asymmetric extraction clearly runs toward Church and Crown. The identity_locked exit option for feud participants reflects that kinship honor is not merely a behavioral choice but a constitutive element of identity. The participant cannot exit without ceasing to be recognizable within the kinship frame — this is different from trapped (external barriers) or constrained (high cost but thinkable). The cognitive frame itself is the binding mechanism.
commentary.perspectival_gap: The perspectival gap reveals the complete range of experienced classification from feud suppression doctrine. The feud participant (powerless/identity_locked) experiences snare: participation is simultaneously obligatory (kinship) and sin (doctrine), with no resolution except spiritual anguish. The kinship group (moderate/constrained) experiences tangled rope: feud coordination solves real deterrence problems, but suppression undermines it without providing alternatives. Church and Crown (institutional/arbitrage) experience rope: the constraint is purely coordinative from their vantage point — they are solving the problem of disorder by redirecting violence through legitimate channels. The nobility (organized/constrained) experience a stratified tangled rope: they coordinate suppression of lower-status feuding (extraction of obedience) while maintaining their own feud rights (self-exemption). Peace guilds (organized/constrained) experience scaffold: feud suppression appears temporary and replaceable by urban commercial enforcement mechanisms. The parish priest (institutional/arbitrage) experiences piton: the enforcement apparatus has degraded into ritual while maintaining institutional inertia. The theological natural law observer (analytical/analytical) risks perceiving mountain: unchangeable divine law forever prohibiting vengeance. The engine's false-summit detector will identify this last perspective as naturalization of a contingent institutional arrangement. The key diagnostic gap: between the beneficiary perspectives (rope, coordination, benefit) and the victim perspective (snare, trapped identity, extraction).
commentary.directionality_logic: Directionality (d values) for each perspective is derived from structural position relative to the feud suppression constraint. Ecclesiastical authority as beneficiary with arbitrage exit: low d (0.15–0.25), derives negative or minimal f(d) — experienced extraction runs away from this agent. Royal authority as beneficiary with arbitrage exit: same derivation, low d. Feud participant as victim with identity_locked exit: high d (0.85–0.92), derives high f(d) (1.15–1.28 range) — experienced extraction is maximal. Kinship group as victim with constrained exit: moderate-high d (0.55–0.65), derives moderate f(d) (0.75–1.00) — significant but not maximal extraction. The identity_locked exit option for feud participants produces higher d than constrained exit for kinship groups because identity-lock is structurally immobilizing: the agent could theoretically refuse but cannot conceive refusal within their identity frame. The constrained exit allows for cost-benefit reasoning; identity-locked does not. Nobility as organized victim with constrained exit: lower d than commoner feuding because nobility retain higher-status feud rights — partial exemption from suppression. The directionality derivation chain automatically produces the right relational structure from beneficiary/victim declarations plus exit options, without requiring manual d calculation. The high chi values for powerless/identity_locked agents and low chi values for institutional/arbitrage agents emerge from the sigmoid function applied to the derived d values, not from arbitrary scaling.
commentary.kernel_context: This constraint instantiates the CHRISTIANIZED PACIFICATION READING of the feud-obligation kernel. The kernel is the contested claim: can blood-debt obligation to kinship coexist with Christian theology prohibiting vengeance, or does one preclude the other? Three readings emit three distinct constraints with different ε values and structural logics. THIS reading (christianized_pacification_reading) measures the constraint as it operates under the institutional claim that feud is sin, vengeance belongs to God alone, and legitimate violence authority is delegated to Church and Crown. The sibling reading (stateless_coordination_reading) measures the constraint from the kinship system's internal logic: feud is legitimate deterrence mechanism solving coordination problems in stateless societies; Church doctrine is external imposition. The third sibling reading (extraction_cycle_reading) measures the constraint as pure extraction by Church and Crown, justified post-hoc with theology that conveniently benefits those enforcing it. Each reading produces different ε, different beneficiary/victim structure, and different comprehension of the kernel itself. The committer frame routes the disagreement about which reading is true (or valid, or discoverable from the material) into omega variables rather than hedging ε or multiplying interpretations within a single story. Each reading stands alone as a clean ε-invariant constraint; the existence of siblings is documented in network.affects_constraints and cs_structure.reading_relations, not mixed into the primary analysis.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: This constraint demonstrates mandatrophy resolution through kernel reading decomposition. The mandatrophy question is: is feud suppression a coordination mechanism (rope) or extraction mechanism (snare), and can these coexist? The answer is: yes, they coexist, but which is dominant depends on which reading of the kernel is adopted. Under the christianized_pacification_reading (this story), feud suppression is tangled_rope: genuine coordination function (reducing violence disorder) combined with asymmetric institutional extraction (Church and Crown gain authority). The mandatrophy is resolved by recognizing that different agents perceive the same structural constraint differently based on their structural position: beneficiaries see coordination (rope), victims see extraction (snare), organized agents see mixed (tangled_rope or scaffold). No single type is correct because the constraint's nature is perspectival — it exists at the intersection of multiple structural relationships. The false-summit mountain perspective reveals that theological naturalization (vengeance belongs to God, a universal law) is actually a contingent institutional arrangement that benefits identifiable beneficiaries. This unmasking is precisely what the mandatrophy apparatus is designed to detect: when a constraint is presented as unchangeable natural law but benefits identifiable institutional agents, the false-summit signature fires and alerts analysis to look for power consolidation mechanisms masked by naturalization.

network.dual_formulation_note: The feud-obligation kernel decomposes into three constraint stories based on reading (interpretation framework). This story (christianized_pacification_reading, ε=0.58, tangled_rope) models the constraint as it operates under Church-Crown institutional framing of feud as sin and delegated violence authority. The stateless_coordination_reading (separate file, expected ε~0.25, rope) models feud as legitimate deterrence mechanism within kinship-based stateless systems. The extraction_cycle_reading (separate file, expected ε~0.72, snare) models feud suppression as pure extraction by rising state-church alliance justified post-hoc with theology. Each reading has a distinct ε value, beneficiary/victim structure, and classification type because each reading identifies different constraint functions and mechanisms. The sibling constraints are related through network.affects_constraints; any analysis of the feud obligation system must account for all three readings and their different structural logics.
